A lead sheet writes swing eighths as plain eighth notes, and that is not an error. The way
they are written is shorthand, the way a chord symbol is. It tells you which notes come where,
and the style tells you how to play them. This lesson covers what the shorthand means, how much
room it leaves you, and how to know when it does *not* mean swing. The two examples are
Oscar Pettiford's *Blues in the Closet*, which swings, and Herbie Hancock's *Watermelon Man*,
which does not.

**How to use the page.** Every example is written out and can be played. Press **▶ Play** to
hear it. Examples that have a **Swing** slider let you set how long the first eighth of each
pair is held, from even (50%) up to a dotted-eighth-and-sixteenth (75%). The **Tempo** box sets
the speed. Play each example at more than one setting before you read on.


## 1. What the page says, and what it means

Here is the first bar of *Blues in the Closet* exactly as a lead sheet writes it.

```{=html}
<div class="sw-ex" data-tempo="120" data-swing="50" data-noslider="1" data-title="As written">
<script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/8
K:F
"F7"F2 AF B2 AF |]
</script></div>
```

Played as written, the eighths are even: each beat is split exactly in half. No jazz player
reads it that way. In a swing tune each pair of eighths is played **long-short**: the note on
the beat is held longer and the note on the "and" comes late. The usual way to explain it is
with a triplet: the beat is split into three, the first note gets two thirds and the second
gets one.

```{=html}
<div class="sw-ex" data-tempo="120" data-swing="50" data-noslider="1" data-title="The triplet explanation (what an arranger would write to be exact)">
<script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/8
K:F
"F7"F2 (3:2:2A2F B2 (3:2:2A2F |]
</script></div>
```

Arrangers almost never write that, because it is hard to read and because, as the rest of this
lesson shows, it is not quite right either. Instead they write plain eighths and put a word or
a sign at the top of the chart:

- **Swing**, **Med. swing**, **Shuffle**, **Bluesy**, or just a tempo and a style name.
- The sign **♫ = ♩ ♪³**: "a pair of eighths equals a quarter and an eighth under a triplet".
- Nothing at all. On a jazz lead sheet, swing is the default, and you are expected to know it.

The one way *not* to read swing eighths is as a dotted eighth and a sixteenth. That is a
ratio of 3 to 1, and at most tempos it sounds stiff and jerky, like a march. Compare it with
the triplet version above.

```{=html}
<div class="sw-ex" data-tempo="120" data-swing="50" data-noslider="1" data-title="Too far: dotted eighth and sixteenth">
<script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/8
K:F
"F7"F2 A>F B2 A>F |]
</script></div>
```

## 2. Swing is a range, not a ratio

The triplet is a useful first picture and a poor final answer. Measurements of recordings
find that players swing anywhere from nearly even to a little past the triplet, and that the
same player changes ratio with the tempo. The rough rule:

<table class="table sw-table">
<thead><tr><th>Tempo</th><th>Typical long:short</th><th>Slider</th><th>What it sounds like</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>Ballad, slow blues (under 80)</td><td>about 2:1, sometimes more</td><td>65–70%</td><td>Lazy, heavy triplet feel, often a 12/8 shuffle</td></tr>
<tr><td>Medium (100–160)</td><td>between 3:2 and 2:1</td><td>62–68%</td><td>The "standard" swing of a blues like <em>Blues in the Closet</em></td></tr>
<tr><td>Up-tempo (over 220)</td><td>close to even</td><td>55–60%</td><td>Eighths almost straight; the swing is in the accents</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

The band on this site follows the same rule: its swing is 68% at 100 beats a minute or slower,
66% at 120, 64% at 160, 60% at 220 and 55% at 300 (the Swing menu's Auto). Try it here. Set the slider to 66% and raise the tempo
to 240: it becomes hard to play and starts to sound like a shuffle. Then lower the slider to
55% at the same tempo.

```{=html}
<div class="sw-ex" data-tempo="132" data-swing="66" data-title="Set the swing yourself">
<script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/8
K:F
"F7"F2 AF B2 AF | "F7"B2 AF- F C2 F- | "F7"F2 AF B2 AF- | "F7"F C3- C2 z F |]
</script></div>
```

### Everything else the shorthand leaves to you

The ratio is only one of the choices a plain line of eighths leaves open. Others matter at least
as much, and the lead sheet says nothing about any of them.

Each choice below shows the line as written, two ways to play it that are both swing, and one
way that is not. The played versions are written out more exactly than any chart would be:
accent marks (>), staccato dots, and "ghost" over a note that is barely played.

With a MIDI keyboard plugged in (Chrome or Edge), **Play it on a keyboard** under any example
counts you in for a bar, records you against a click, and says how you did: your swing ratio for
the tempo, which notes you leaned on, ghosts, note lengths and ties, how far ahead of or behind
the click you sat, and any notes you moved by an eighth.

#### Accents on the off-beats

Swing players lean on the "and", not the beat. A line of eighths is usually played
*doo-BAH doo-BAH*, with the beat note soft and the off-beat note pushed. This is why fast swing
still swings at nearly even eighths.

```{=html}
<div class="sw-ex" data-tempo="132" data-swing="62" data-noslider="1" data-title="As written">
<script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/8
K:F
"F7"FA cA dc AF | "Bb7"D2 FA- A4 |]
</script></div>
<div class="sw-ex" data-tempo="132" data-swing="62" data-noslider="1" data-title="✓ Accent every &quot;and&quot; (doo-BAH doo-BAH)">
<script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/8
K:F
"F7"F!>!A c!>!A d!>!c A!>!F | "Bb7"D2 F!>!A- A4 |]
</script></div>
<div class="sw-ex" data-tempo="132" data-swing="62" data-noslider="1" data-title="✓ Accent only the off-beats that start or turn the line">
<script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/8
K:F
"F7"F!>!A cA dc A!>!F | "Bb7"D2 F!>!A- A4 |]
</script></div>
<div class="sw-ex" data-tempo="132" data-swing="62" data-noslider="1" data-title="✗ Accent every beat (DOO-bah DOO-bah): a march, however long-short it is">
<script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/8
K:F
"F7"!>!FA !>!cA !>!dc !>!AF | "Bb7"!>!D2 FA- A4 |]
</script></div>
```

#### Ghosted notes

A note in the middle of a run may be barely played at all, more felt than heard.

```{=html}
<div class="sw-ex" data-tempo="132" data-swing="62" data-noslider="1" data-title="As written">
<script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/8
K:F
"F7"cB AG FG Ac | "Bb7"d4 z4 |]
</script></div>
<div class="sw-ex" data-tempo="132" data-swing="62" data-noslider="1" data-title="✓ Ghost one note on a beat in the middle of the run">
<script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/8
K:F
"F7"cB "^ghost"!pp!A!f!G FG Ac | "Bb7"d4 z4 |]
</script></div>
<div class="sw-ex" data-tempo="132" data-swing="62" data-noslider="1" data-title="✓ Ghost two notes on beats, so the line seems to skip down">
<script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/8
K:F
"F7"cB "^ghost"!pp!A!f!G "^ghost"!pp!F!f!G Ac | "Bb7"d4 z4 |]
</script></div>
<div class="sw-ex" data-tempo="132" data-swing="62" data-noslider="1" data-title="✗ Ghost the note the line is heading for: the melody goes missing">
<script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/8
K:F
"F7"cB AG FG Ac | "Bb7""^ghost"!pp!d4 z4 |]
</script></div>
```

#### Length

A written quarter note is often played short (*dit*), especially on beats 2 and 4 and at the
end of a phrase. A written eighth tied over the bar line is played long.

```{=html}
<div class="sw-ex" data-tempo="132" data-swing="62" data-noslider="1" data-title="As written">
<script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/8
K:F
"F7"z2 A2 z2 c2 | "Bb7"z2 dc A2 F2- | "F7"F8 |]
</script></div>
<div class="sw-ex" data-tempo="132" data-swing="62" data-noslider="1" data-title="✓ Quarters on 2 and 4 short (dit), the tied note held full">
<script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/8
K:F
"F7"z2 .A2 z2 .c2 | "Bb7"z2 dc .A2 F2- | "F7"F8 |]
</script></div>
<div class="sw-ex" data-tempo="132" data-swing="62" data-noslider="1" data-title="✓ Quarters held (doo), the tied note let go after beat 2">
<script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/8
K:F
"F7"z2 !tenuto!A2 z2 !tenuto!c2 | "Bb7"z2 dc !tenuto!A2 F2- | "F7"F4 z4 |]
</script></div>
<div class="sw-ex" data-tempo="132" data-swing="62" data-noslider="1" data-title="✗ The tie dropped: the F played again on beat 1 instead of held over the bar line">
<script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/8
K:F
"F7"z2 .A2 z2 .c2 | "Bb7"z2 dc .A2 F2 | "F7"F8 |]
</script></div>
```

#### Where in the beat

Some players sit right on the beat, others play a fraction behind it ("laid back") against a
drummer who is on top of it. Neither is written; both are swing. Laid back is far smaller than
any written note value; the sixteenth rest below is an exaggeration so it can be seen.

```{=html}
<div class="sw-ex" data-tempo="120" data-swing="62" data-noslider="1" data-title="As written (and ✓ played on top of the beat)">
<script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/16
K:F
"F7"F4 A2F2 B4 A2F2 | "F7"C8 z8 |]
</script></div>
<div class="sw-ex" data-tempo="120" data-swing="50" data-noslider="1" data-title="✓ Laid back (exaggerated): every note a hair late, the bar lines where they were">
<script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/16
K:F
"F7"z F3 zA zF zB3 zA zF | "F7"z C7 z8 |]
</script></div>
<div class="sw-ex" data-tempo="120" data-swing="62" data-noslider="1" data-title="✗ So far behind that the beat notes land on the &quot;and&quot;: the line has moved, not leaned">
<script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/16
K:F
"F7"z2 F4 A2F2 B4 A2 | "F7"F2 C8 z6 |]
</script></div>
```

#### Small changes to the rhythm

Players anticipate a note by an eighth, delay one, or add a pickup. On a lead sheet, that is
interpretation, not a wrong note.

```{=html}
<div class="sw-ex" data-tempo="132" data-swing="62" data-noslider="1" data-title="As written">
<script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/8
K:F
"F7"z4 A2 c2 | "Bb7"d4 c2 A2 | "F7"F8 |]
</script></div>
<div class="sw-ex" data-tempo="132" data-swing="62" data-noslider="1" data-title="✓ Anticipate: the d and the last F come an eighth early, tied over">
<script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/8
K:F
"F7"z4 A2 cd- | "Bb7"d4 c2 AF- | "F7"F8 |]
</script></div>
<div class="sw-ex" data-tempo="132" data-swing="62" data-noslider="1" data-title="✓ Add a pickup into the phrase and delay the c by an eighth">
<script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/8
K:F
"F7"z2 FG A2 zc | "Bb7"d4 c2 A2 | "F7"F8 |]
</script></div>
<div class="sw-ex" data-tempo="132" data-swing="62" data-noslider="1" data-title="✗ The whole phrase a beat late: the long notes now fall on 2, and it ends in the next bar">
<script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/8
K:F
"F7"z6 A2 | "Bb7"c2 d4 c2 | "F7"A2 F6 |]
</script></div>
```

What is *not* up to you: where the bar lines are, where the notes fall in the beat (on it or on
the "and"), and the form. A swing eighth on the "and" of 2 is late, but it is still the "and"
of 2.

## 3. Blues in the Closet

*Blues in the Closet* is a medium-tempo jazz blues, usually played somewhere between 120 and
180 beats a minute. Here is the whole melody, in F, as it is written in the tune library.

```{=html}
<div class="sw-ex" data-tempo="132" data-swing="64" data-title="Blues in the Closet (Oscar Pettiford)">
<script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/4
K:F
F/-| "F7"F A/F/ B A/F/ | "F7"B A/F/- F/ C F/- | "F7"F A/F/ B A/F/- | "F7" F/ C3/2-C z/ F/-|
"Bb7"F _A/F/ B A/F/ | "Bb7"B _A/F/- F/ C F/- | "F7"F =A/F/ B A/F/- | "F7" F/ C3/2-C z/ F/-|
"Gm7"F A/F/ B A/F/ | "C7"B A/F/- F/ C F/- | "F7"F A/F/ B A/F/- | "C7"F2 z2 |]
</script></div>
```

There is no "Swing" marking on it, and none is needed: it is a bebop-era blues, every
recording of it swings, and the eighth-note pairs are written the way every jazz player
expects. Play it at 50% and then at 64% to hear what the marking would have told you.

### The places that change when it swings

- **The pickup and the ties.** The tune starts on the "and" of 4 and ties it into the bar. In
  swing, that pickup is late (it is the short note of a pair), so the first note of the tune
  arrives *just* before the bar line and pulls the band into it. The same figure ends bars 4
  and 8. These anticipations are the strongest swing feature in the tune: give them a little
  accent.
- **The figure *A F*.** In every bar the melody drops from the 3rd to the root in a pair of
  eighths. Swung, it is *long-short*, and the short F is the one to lean on.
- **The tied F in bar 2.** *A/F/- F/ C* is four eighths, with the second tied to the third.
  Swung, the tied F lands on the late "and" of 2 and sustains through beat 3. Played even, the
  syncopation is weaker and the bar sounds square.
- **The long notes.** The C in bars 4 and 8 is a dotted quarter tied to a quarter. It can be
  held full length or cut off early; both are common. The rest that follows is where the
  rhythm section, or another player, answers.

### A range of good readings

Three players reading the same lead sheet would not play the same thing, and all three would be
right. Try these settings and decide which one you like:

<table class="table sw-table">
<thead><tr><th>Setting</th><th>Tempo</th><th>Slider</th><th>Feel</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>Relaxed</td><td>120</td><td>66–68%</td><td>Close to the triplet, heavy, bluesy</td></tr>
<tr><td>Medium</td><td>150</td><td>62–66%</td><td>The usual jam-session reading</td></tr>
<tr><td>Up</td><td>220+</td><td>55–60%</td><td>Nearly even; put the swing in accents on the off-beats</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

What no setting allows is 50% at a medium tempo with every note accented equally. That is the
one clear misreading.

## 4. Watermelon Man: eighths that do not swing

*Watermelon Man* (from *Takin' Off*, 1962) is also a blues, with 16 bars instead of 12, and it
is written in exactly the same way: plain eighth notes, no triplets, no dots. Here are its
first eight bars and the four-bar riff that follows.

```{=html}
<div class="sw-ex" data-tempo="126" data-swing="50" data-title="Watermelon Man (Herbie Hancock), bars 1 to 12">
<script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/8
K:F
"F7"_e8- | "F7"e2 FF c d2 F- | "F7"F8- | "F7"F8 |
"Bb7"f8- | "Bb7"f2 FF c d2 F- | "F7"F8- | "F7"F8 |
"C7"z2 cc g2 a2 | "Bb7"_ag fd f2 g2 | "C7"z2 cc g2 a2 | "Bb7"_ag fd f2 d2 |]
</script></div>
```

On the page it looks like *Blues in the Closet*: eighth notes, ties over the bar line,
anticipations. The difference is the style. This is a **straight-eighth** tune: the eighths
are even, and they stay even when the tempo drops. It is often marked "Funky", "Latin", "Even
8ths" or "Straight 8ths", but on many lead sheets it is not marked at all, and you are
expected to know it from the record, the same as with a swing tune.

Now move the slider to 66% and play it again. Bars 9 to 12 suffer most: *z2 cc g2 a2* starts on
an off-beat pair, and swinging it turns a crisp, funky riff into something closer to a
nursery rhyme. The off-beat F in bars 2 and 6, which should snap against the beat, goes soft.

### "Somewhere between"

Even this tune is not perfectly even. Hancock said that Billy Higgins played it "somewhere
between straight eighth notes and the swinging triplets of jazz". That is a slider setting of
perhaps 53 to 56%, which is not enough to sound like swing but is enough to keep the line from
sounding mechanical. Mongo Santamaría's hit version a year later is a cha-cha, and its eighths
are straight. Both are good readings of the same lead sheet; a 66% swing is not.

So the range of acceptable readings exists for straight tunes too. It is just centred in a
different place.

## 5. The contrast, side by side

<table class="table sw-table">
<thead><tr><th></th><th><em>Blues in the Closet</em></th><th><em>Watermelon Man</em></th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>Written as</td><td>Plain eighths</td><td>Plain eighths</td></tr>
<tr><td>Played as</td><td>Swing, long-short</td><td>Even, or very nearly</td></tr>
<tr><td>Slider</td><td>55–68%, by tempo</td><td>50–56%</td></tr>
<tr><td>Where the energy is</td><td>Accents on the off-beats, late pickups</td><td>Crisp, equal subdivisions locked to a backbeat or a Latin pattern</td></tr>
<tr><td>How you know</td><td>Jazz blues, bebop era, every recording</td><td>The record, the style ("funk", "Latin", "even 8ths")</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

The point is that **the notation is identical**. Everything that separates these two tunes in
performance comes from outside the notes: the style, the era, the recording and the band.

## 6. Reading a new lead sheet

When you open a chart you have not played before, before you play a note:

1. **Look at the top of the page** for a style or feel word, a ♫ = ♩ ♪³ sign, or "even 8ths".
2. **Look at the tempo.** The faster it is, the straighter the swing.
3. **Know where the tune comes from.** A jazz standard or a bebop blues swings unless told
   otherwise. A funk, Latin, rock, soul or bossa nova tune does not.
4. **Listen to a recording.** It is the only thing that settles the question, and it tells you
   about the accents and the note lengths too, which no lead sheet shows.
5. **Listen to the band.** If the drummer plays the swing ride pattern, match its ratio; if the
   drummer plays straight eighths on the hi-hat, play straight. The ratio is shared, not
   chosen alone.

Then practise both tunes in this lesson at three tempos each, and play the slider settings from
the tables until you can hear the difference without looking.

```{=html}
<script src="/apps/shared/soundfont.js"></script>
<script src="/apps/shared/abcjs-basic.js?v=2"></script>
<script src="/apps/shared/midi-feel.js?v=2"></script>
<script>
// Each .sw-ex holds an ABC tune in a <script type="text/plain">; render it and give it Play, Tempo and (unless
// data-noslider) a Swing slider. Playback is abcjs's synth with its `swing` option (50 = even, 66 = triplet, 75 = dotted).
(function () {
  var ac = null, current = null;
  function ratio(p) { var r = p / (100 - p); return p <= 50 ? 'even (1:1)' : p >= 74 ? 'dotted (3:1)' : r.toFixed(2).replace(/0$/, '') + ':1' + (Math.abs(p - 66.7) < 1.5 ? ' (triplet)' : ''); }
  function stop() { if (current) { current.synth.stop(); current.btn.textContent = '▶ Play'; current = null; } }
  Array.prototype.forEach.call(document.querySelectorAll('.sw-ex'), function (ex, i) {
    var abc = ex.querySelector('script').textContent.trim();
    var swing = +(ex.dataset.swing || 50), tempo = +(ex.dataset.tempo || 120);
    var html = '<div class="sw-title">' + (ex.dataset.title || '') + '</div><div class="sw-staff" id="sw-staff-' + i + '"></div>' +
      '<div class="sw-tools"><button type="button" class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-secondary sw-play">▶ Play</button>' +
      '<span><label for="sw-t-' + i + '">Tempo</label><input type="number" id="sw-t-' + i + '" min="40" max="300" step="4" value="' + tempo + '"></span>';
    if (!ex.dataset.noslider) html += '<span><label for="sw-s-' + i + '">Swing</label><input type="range" id="sw-s-' + i + '" min="50" max="75" step="1" value="' + swing + '"></span>' +
      '<span class="sw-ratio"></span><span class="sw-presets"><button type="button" class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-secondary" data-p="50">Even</button> <button type="button" class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-secondary" data-p="60">3:2</button> <button type="button" class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-secondary" data-p="67">Triplet</button> <button type="button" class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-secondary" data-p="75">Dotted</button></span>';
    html += '</div>';
    ex.insertAdjacentHTML('beforeend', html);
    var vo = ABCJS.renderAbc('sw-staff-' + i, abc, { responsive: 'resize', add_classes: true })[0];
    var btn = ex.querySelector('.sw-play'), slider = ex.querySelector('input[type=range]'), tIn = ex.querySelector('input[type=number]'), out = ex.querySelector('.sw-ratio');
    function show() { if (out) out.textContent = slider.value + '% — ' + ratio(+slider.value); }
    if (slider) { slider.addEventListener('input', function () { show(); if (current && current.ex === ex) play(); }); show(); }
    Array.prototype.forEach.call(ex.querySelectorAll('.sw-presets .btn'), function (b) { b.addEventListener('click', function () { slider.value = b.dataset.p; show(); play(); }); });
    function play() {
      stop();
      ac = ac || new (window.AudioContext || window.webkitAudioContext)();
      ac.resume();
      var synth = new ABCJS.synth.CreateSynth(), me = { synth: synth, btn: btn, ex: ex };
      current = me; btn.textContent = '■ Stop';
      getSoundfontUrl().then(function (url) {
        return synth.init({ audioContext: ac, visualObj: vo, millisecondsPerMeasure: 4 * 60000 / (+tIn.value || tempo),
          options: { soundFontUrl: url, swing: slider ? +slider.value : swing, chordsOff: false, program: 0,
            onEnded: function () { if (current === me) { btn.textContent = '▶ Play'; current = null; } } } });
      }).then(function () { return synth.prime(); }).then(function () { if (current === me) synth.start(); })
        .catch(function (e) { btn.textContent = '▶ Play'; console.error(e); });
    }
    btn.addEventListener('click', function () { if (current && current.ex === ex) stop(); else play(); });
    if (window.MidiFeel) MidiFeel.attach(ex, { abc: abc, getBpm: function () { return +tIn.value || tempo; } });
  });
})();
</script>
```
